title: 2 · Transactions, ACID & Concurrency Problems (Unit 3)
learn:
Transaction

A transaction is a program unit whose execution may change the contents of the database, a logical unit of work that must complete entirely to stay correct. Example: transfer 100 from A (300) to B (400): Read A, A=A-100, Write A, Read B, B=B+100, Write B. Before: 300+400 = 700. After: 200+500 = 700, consistent.

ACID

Atomicity: all or nothing (commit makes changes visible, abort hides them). Consistency: a consistent database stays consistent (sum before = sum after). Isolation: a transaction's actions are hidden from others until it terminates. Durability: once committed, updates are permanent.

Why run transactions concurrently?

Shorter waiting time and better throughput and resource use. The price is four classic problems:

1. Lost update (W-W): x=100. T1 reads 100, T2 reads 100, T1 writes 110, T2 writes 80: T1's update is overwritten.
2. Dirty read / temporary update (W-R): T1 writes x=110 then fails, but T2 already read 110 and built on it.
3. Incorrect summary: T2 sums A and Y while T1 changes Y in between, so the total mixes old and new values.
4. Unrepeatable read (R-W): T1 reads A=1000, T2 changes A to 3000, T1 reads again and gets 3000.

Implementing atomicity and durability

The recovery manager does it. The simple shadow-database scheme keeps a db_pointer to the current copy; all updates go to a new copy. Abort: ignore the new copy. Commit: flip the pointer to the new copy. It assumes one transaction at a time and no disk failure, so it does not handle concurrency.

quiz.q: Which ACID property says a transaction is all or nothing?
quiz.why: Commit or abort, nothing in between.

quiz.q: T1 writes x, fails, but T2 already read x. This is a?
Two transactions overwrite each other's writes. This is a?
T1 reads A twice and gets different values because T2 changed it. This is?
In the shadow-database scheme, commit means?
options: Move db_pointer to the new copy
Copy the old into the new

quiz.q: Which is NOT an advantage of concurrent execution?
quiz.why: Conflicts are the cost, so we need control.

lab.task: A=500, B=200. T1 moves 100 from A to B. Show why T2 printing A+B halfway gives an inconsistent total, and name the problem.
lab.solution: If T2 reads after W(A)=400 but before W(B)=300, it sees 400+200 = 600 instead of 700. This is an incorrect summary (violates isolation).
